chunks: Your Lord is God who created the heavens and the earth in six spans, then assumed His power, dispensing all affairs. None can intercede with Him except by His leave. He is God, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not be warned?
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about Allah's creation, His Throne, and the condition for intercession?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Yunus identifies Allah as the Creator of the heavens and the earth who established Himself upon the Throne and manages all affairs. It highlights the concept of intercession being contingent upon His permission and calls upon believers to worship Him alone. In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to affirm Allah's sovereignty and the exclusive nature of divine authority, reinforcing the principle that all intercessors act only by His leave.
